[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61634846][b]August 1, 2028: Soldiers[/b]

[spoiler]The first order had arrived before sunrise, awakening the commander of the 3rd Thývenic Infantry Brigade, it told him to go westward. Then at breakfast another command came, ordering him to stay put, this one from a different official, then another telling him to go southward to join the forces massing in Mittlemarkke.

Iseg Radwell now sat in his office peering out the window where the soldiers, trucks, and other vehicles were being readied to deploy to wherever the last order had stated.

He hadnt surmised yet the worst case scenario, and that was the total collapse of any form of hierarchy, he had already known of four units within Thýven which had apparently abandoned their posts and gone home once the declaration of war had been issued, he already knew that some within his own brigade were plotting a similar manner.

However, Iseg had vowed to serve Rosenmarkke thirty years prior, and while the regime was insane, the protection of the citizens was paramount regardless of the state.

As he watched out of the window blinds a young soldier walked in, a staffer really, he held an envelope. 

Give it, stated Iseg not turning from the window as the soldier walked forward and handed it to him, nodding he dismissed the fellow and opened the letter, his brow furrowed immediately.

[i]NOTICE: All contact with Knygta and Deyn has ceased, it is believed that local command centers are being hijacked, standby for further order.[/i]

Dropping the letter on his desk he moved out of the office, walking briskly down the hall and into the command yard, I want a full review he snapped at one of the officers, who began ordering the troops to get into formation for a review.

Where are the trucks? Asked Iseg looking for the convoy trucks.

They left, replied a soldier who was standing by.

Where?! Demanded Iseg.

The soldier shrugged.

The yard soon filled with troops and movement, headcounts had begun, they were missing several soldiers and a few officers.

Sir, said a voice, Iseg spun around as he saw the radio operator rush up to him.

What?! Demanded Isag, Spit it out!

The radios are being jammed, we cannot establish communications with central command, 

Iseg frowned, something had gone terribly wrong, Can we identify where the jamming is coming from? 

No sir, most likely within the region though, 

Iseg pursed his lips, turned to one of his officers and shook his head, How many do we have? He asked.

We are missing about 1/4th sir, replied the officer.

Iseg nodded, Send them back to their posts, the barracks, whatever, we will wait for a more conclusive set of orders, before walking back to his office.

[b]Haakon Strømm: Spirals[/b]

Were losing the islands, intoned Iosef Begren grimly.

You assured me they were secure, replied Haakon quietly.

We underestimated the local ground movement, and our overreach, replied Begren.

Haakon nodded, We shouldve arrested the duc, 

Are the Montfleurois aware? He asked.

I am not sure, replied Begren, The SCSID just doesnt have the manpower right now, replied Begren.

Haakon sighed, Shut down the internet, jam all non-essential radio comms, close the borders, 

That would make matters far worse sir, replied Begren.

Do it, I dont give a d-mn, the central army will handle it, waved Haakon.

Begren nodded, and left the room.

[b]Montfleur: A flurry of info[/b]

Your majesty, the Gendarme has stopped a convoy of trucks from Rosenmarkke attempting to cross our border, the soldiers surrendered upon reaching the border and are in custody of the state, began General Louis De Funes, head of the Gendarme.

Henri nodded as Eleonore took notes, leaning back in his chair, How are the islands, he asked looking at the head of General Security Directorate, Peter Jalouse.

Intel suggests that the duc has cut off communications, local militias have been activated, and there seems to be plans to storm one of the remaining bases on the island, replied Jalouse.

Henri pursed his lips and nodded again, Good, any word from the regime?

None, sir, replied Jalouse, Although there seems to be some decohesion in the forces in Thýven, 

Sir, theyve cut the internet, piped up one of the aides as they looked up from an telecom pad that had been laid on the table.

Henri smiled, It seems the regime is afraid, how long do you give the state Peter? 

Sir, at this rate, if Knygta and Deyn secedes as they alerted us, and does so without issue, we expect Westmarkke, Thýven, and Belgarde to follow within the next few days to weeks, he replied.

Will we need boots in Rosenmarkke? asked Henri of Louis.

Only once the first regions secede and request union, replied the aged general.

Could we put boots on the islands? asked Henri.

The general shook his head, Not without suppressing the abilities of the ground forces of the mainland, they still have submarine capabilities, and due to how rapidly the situation is forming, well wed have to wait days to a week perhaps to deploy a formal defensive/offensive force, 

Henri frowned and looked at Eleonore, What is your take? 

Eleonore looked up from her notepad, Belgarde we could get troops in, I am aware that our largest base of support is there, and the commander of the regional forces has actually been in contact with me already, he is good friends with the duc. But as for a naval expedition, its several thousand kilometers around the coast.

What is the situation in Belgarde, director? Asked Henri of Peter.

Last we checked, stable, they are expected to be a staging ground for any forces, replied Peter.

Eleonore, would the assembly support an immediate unionisation of Belgarde? If we can legally integrate them into the state as soon as possible, then any troop movements would constitute an invasion of our sovereign territory, 

Eleonore nodded, Its hard to say, wed have to assure them that Belgarde is doing this of their own will,

Phones are down, stated the aide once more.

Sir, stated another aide, stepping into the room, The Bojerries has arrived,

Henri smiled, Ah good, lunch for all of us, we need it, he stood up and clapped. 

After a few moments of discussions a tray of fast food was brought into the room, filling the room with the smell of fried chicken, another tray of Nuka Kola cans was also brought in and, Henri began handing them out as the officers and aides filled their paper plates with food.

See, unlike the Rosenmarkket leadership, we here in Montfleur like a good time, even in situations of dire importance, stated Henri, opening his vicodin bottle and popping a pill in, screwing the lid tight.

[b]August 2, 2028: Secession[/b]

Albert Iverkjthing stood quietly in his bedroom, the morning sunlight peeking through the closed curtains that hung on his window. Comms had been cut with the government and militias had been raised, the government had made haste to cut the internet, the phones, however, thanks to the redundancy of the government, they had failed to remember the emergency telegraph lines which had been laid across the country in the event all major communications had been cut by an enemy. Now, Knygta and Deyn was using it against them to relay orders to the various defecting groups on the mainland.

Albert had unwillingly become the leader of the secessionist movement, he rose from the bed, stretched, and began to dress himself, looking in the mirror he frowned, what would come next? Could the state recover from such an action, would Haakon unleash the army against the islands?

He had been assured that the navy was weak, incapable, and that any response would be weak, after all, the war with Wuloosya had ravaged the major infrastructure of the islands, but, concerns had risen that the SCSID would be able to launch a precision attack to end the movement instantaneously.

He left the room, went downstairs, and left the house, stepping onto the street, he noted how quiet the city was, once the busiest city in Rosenmarkke, the economic hub, the streets had gone silent. He would have to walk, the electricity had gone out and the subway wasnt working.

As he walked down the street, passerbys stopped and stared, pointing at him in hushed whispers, he noted civilians and militia members dressed in camo raided from outpost stores and surplus stores as well as attics and basements across the island. These militia members wore a distinctive blue and yellow armband.

Arriving at the office of the duc of Knygta and Deyn, he looked out the window onto the large square that faced the office, a crowd had begun to gather, he was expected to formally declare secession in an hour to the whole world.

Withdrawing from his desk the crumpled speech he had prepared, he read through it, smoothing its edges out. After an hour, the time came, his aide walked in, nodded, and two members of the militia moved to open the doors that led to the balcony, Albert stepped out.

The roar of the crowd hit him like a wave, cheers and clapping filled the area as signs and flags were waved, some pro-unionist, some independence, and some just there. He waved to the crowd and stepped forward to the microphones that had been set up.

My people and foreigners and workers and all members of this nation, welcome,

I stand before you today, on this momentous occasion, to declare to the world, to the regime, and to all people who tune their ears to listen. Freedom has won, freedom will win, freedom will forever win. 

From the earliest days of these islands, we have prided ourselves in our rugged individualism, our culture, and our republican heritage. We have stood as the heart of Rosenmarkke since before Rosenmarkke existed. 

And thus, as we see the nation crumbling day by day, we must take matters into our own hands. We must fight against the forces of tyranny that assail themselves against our homes, our families, our workplaces. We must fight against the forces of despotism that threaten to undermine the global order, and destroy our individuality. We must fight against Strømmism and individualistic politics. We must fight.

It is with this declaration, that we will fight, on the beaches, in the sea, we will fight until there is no longer a fight left in us. 

Knygta and Deyn, I declare you free!

The crowd roared with support as the last words echoed over the crowd, the church bells began to ring in the city as music began to play and a group of militiamen rushed to tear down the Rosenmarkket flag from the pole that stood in the center of the square. [/spoiler]

[b]August 4, 2028: Hell on Erene[/b]

[b]The Sallacher Invasion[/b]

Henri sat at the table with his advisers and Eleonore, video footage of Knygta and Deyn playing across the wide screen televisions that lined the walls of the situation room.

Knygta and Deyn just seceded yesterday, and nowwe have a former medieval duchy or principality, invading a former duchy, stated Henri slowly trying to process the events of that morning.

Yes sir, replied General De Funes.

Henri sighed, Do we have a ground situation on Belgarde? 

Sallach forces entered the duchy last night, numbering approximately 6,000 with a tank division, replied De Funes, They managed to secure two airfields approximately 20 and 30 kilometers from the border, 

What about resistance? Asked Henri.

Given the speed at which they traversed 20 to 30 kilometers, Id say none, replied De Funes.

Any word from the regime? 

The regime, your majesty, has been slow to react, we suspect a lack of resources or thinly stretched resources, as well as cooperation on the level of the government of Belgarde, replied Jalouse.

Henri nodded, While this wasnt in our plan book, well roll with it, General De Funes, prepare a back up contingency of 7,000 Gendarmerie and two tank divisions,

The general nodded and stood up to make some phone calls.

[b]The biggest crashout[/b]

WHERE ARE THE SOLDIERS! Screamed Haakon Strømm as word of the Sallach incursion reached him.

They havent been able to centralise yet, replied Begren, The situation is changing too fast,

Dont we have bombers?! Demanded Haakon.

We can deploy them, replied Begren.

Then bomb these troops to sh-t commander!

Begren nodded and left the room to order any airforce pilots or commanders still loyal to the regime to scramble their jets.

As Begren walked out of the office and down the hall, an officer approached him, stopping and saluting him. He spoke, Sir, we have received reports that the administration in Belgarde intends to surrender to Sallach, they complain that there is little aide from the central command and that there is little ability to coordinate. 

Bergen scoffed as he began walking down the hall once more, motioning for the officer to follow him.

Are you aware of the rules of combat sir? Asked Begren.

A little, I was taught them at the academie, replied the officer.

Then you are familiar with the laws and regulations regarding combatants, continued Begren.

Yes, replied the officer.

What do you think secessionists count as? Pressed Begren.

Enemies of the state? Asked the officer unsure.

Bingo, ergo, they are lawful combatants, replied Begren, Especially if they have formed militias,
Sir I do not understand, how does this relate to the situation at hand? asked the officer.

Well, youll see, you will see, replied Begren with a grim smile.

[b]The Command[/b]

Lieutenant Wjlliam House could feel the power of the F-35 rumbling along the strip of the tarmac at Haakon E. Roelffe Airbase, located in Mittlemarkke approximately 50 km from the capital in the north.

The situation on the ground was chaotic, apparently Mittlemarkke was one of the few regions where commands and orders were actually reaching soldiers, primarily due to the internet and comms shutdown affecting the channels the armed forces usually used during situations like these.

However, his superiors had assured him and his airmen that there would be full restoration of connectivity within the next twenty four hours, as the SCSID had begun to activate its special command channels.

House pushed on the throttle as the control tower chattered into his earpiece, he leaned slightly back in the seat, and the plane throttled forward down the runway reaching a breakneck speed as it lifted off.

Upon reaching the desired altitude, House turned towards Belgarde, asking for a clarification on the coordinates of the forces he was required to strike, they were repeated to him twice. 

As he breached the border of Belgarde, the comms sprung to life once again, this time a different voice spoke, There has been an attempted attack by the Sallach forces, they have breached the city of Wavre, and are attacking the royal palace, evacuations in place, 

House shrugged off the information, unsure whether the comm had been meant for someone else or was merely an update, he turned northwards, towards the region where he had been told the forces were expected to be found, beginning a short descent to get within firing range.

The comms crackled on Wavre-23, turn to Wavre, 

House frowned, he knew Wavre, it was a dense medieval city, there was no way that they expected him to bomb any location within the city, unless the ground forces had managed to evacuate citizens.

Wavre-23, turn to Wavre repeated the order.

Can I get a clarification on that order? asked House.

Wavre-23, repeated the voice, Turn to Wavre, CENTCOM, fire at the given target, Sallach forces in city, 

House turned the plane, noting out of his cockpit another plane, the same model as his had joined him, the pilot gave him a thumbs up, Were turning to Wavre, said the voice of the pilot over his headset.

Yea, I know, I dont know why, replied House as the fighter planes continued onwards

They descended lower as the outskirts of Wavre came into view, Its the city square ya? asked House.

Yes, replied the other pilot, I am readying my missiles, 

House frowned, On the count of 3 right? he asked.

Yes, replied the other pilot, the centre of the city appeared, the cathedral of Wavre standing tall over the main square, a massive crowd had formed in the square.

1 began the other pilot, Houses finger hovered over the release trigger, those werent soldiers, 2 continued the other pilot, Bombs away! declared the other pilot as House immediately jerked the plane away from teh city centre, hearing the massive explosions as they hit the square from a distance, the other plane continuing on a straight course before banking back towards the base it had come from.

[b]Belgarde[/b]

Antoine Jacques strolled through the halls of the ducal palace, he had been placed as the temporary regional administrator of Belgarde following the arrest of the duc, and had spent very few days in office.

The morning of August 2nd had come as a shock to him as Knygta and Deyn declared effective independence from Rosenmarkke. His mind had lept to the secessionist movement in Belgarde and their reaction, predicting to the general of the Central Belgarde Forces (which had been ordered under the centralisation order days earlier) that protests would most certainly sweep the region in the following days.

However, he had not expected a full northern invasion by the principality of Sallach, as such, he had risen from the office of the duc and begun to wander the halls, his cane tapping the carpet, head bent in thought.

The regime was unstable and rapidly collapsing, only the loyalty of the remaining ducs and the armed forces mattered in any form of preservation, and these acted only as temporary forces of preservation.

If perhaps he surrendered to the Sallach forces they would provide an amnesty agreement for his involvement in the regime, however, where Sallach moved, Montfleur was bound to follow.

Then there were the protests, he stopped to listen to the growing roar in the palace square, the protests were closer than the Sallach army, and he had ordered the guards to show maximum restraint.

The sound of jets roared over the palace, the palace suddenly shook violently as windows suddenly burst indward, the roar of the crowd suddenly turned into chaotic screams

Antoine found himself knocked over against a table shielding his face from the bits of glass that showered the hall as he espied thick smoke from the square.

Staggering to the broken window he espied half the square covered in gore and soot, half of a building blown to bits as the surviving protestors fled with some attempting to drag the wounded out of the carnage.

The bastard government had bombed their own citizens, Antoine clutched the wall, as the scene unfolded before him, palace aides rushing into the hallway to drag him from the window.

Bastardes! Shouted Antoine, This is not the eternal revolution! This is massacre! 

[b]The Bombing[/b]

Henri sat in shock as news flowed in that the Rosenmarkket regime had ordered the bombing of a group of protesters in Belgarde.

They did what?! Half shouted Eleonore.

Apparently according to some of our sources, the initial command was to bomb the Sallach forces, someone changed the command, replied the aide.

Do we know who?! Asked Henri.

We suspect Begren, your majesty,

Id assume it was to try and dissuade any secession movement, replied Henri.

Most likely, but the intelligence have received a communication that the temporary administration of Belgarde wants to talk, replied the aide

Oh, so now they want to talk, scoffed Henri, After bombing their own protestors,

And some pilot went along with this?! Asked Eleonore.

We do not know,

Henri placed his face into his hands and sighed frustratedly.

Wed be willing to engage in talks with the administration of Belgarde, but, I am not stopping Sallach from advancing, replied Eleonore.

Well they might not have an option to stop, the localised armies have been fleeing or have been surrendering, replied the aide.

Rosenmarkke shouldnt be collapsing this fast, however, replied Henri.

No, we never expected this, replied Eleonore.
